section_summary: An Argentine decree restores the Japanese Association in Argentina’s legal status on humanitarian grounds, subject to changes in its membership and activities. A record-copy form follows, then an embassy despatch about the reorganization of a Japanese relief committee and an airgram requesting copies of a Tokyo despatch.

subfiles.title: Decree No. 931 restoring the Japanese Association in Argentina’s legal status
subfiles.doc_type: translated decree enclosed with a despatch
subfiles.about: The decree annuls an earlier measure against the association while requiring changes to its statutes and membership rules.
subfiles.summary: Citing the association’s charitable work and Cosquín sanatorium, the decree restores its legal status. It requires equal rights for Argentine members, limits activities to statutory purposes, and excludes people deemed a threat to national or regional security.

subfiles.title: Record-copy replacement form
subfiles.about: The form designates an attached despatch copy to replace an original action copy that was not returned.
subfiles.summary: Designates a replacement record copy and directs its return for filing.

subfiles.title: Reorganization of Japanese Committee for Relief to Japan
subfiles.from: R. Kenneth Oakley, for the Chargé d’Affaires ad interim, Buenos Aires
subfiles.about: The embassy reports that a Japanese relief committee has removed people it found objectionable and may soon send relief shipments.
subfiles.summary: The embassy confirms the committee’s reorganization and expects relief shipments from Argentina to proceed soon. It refers to earlier concern that relief groups could revive Japanese imperialism.

subfiles.title: Request for additional copies of a Tokyo despatch
subfiles.about: The embassy requests additional copies of a despatch from the U.S. Political Adviser at Tokyo for possible delivery to the Foreign Office.
subfiles.summary: Requests copies of Tokyo despatch No. 1047, dated May 9, 1947.
